newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch KLM in flight deal with Holland Intl.
newsitem.headline: Dutch KLM in flight deal with Holland Intl.

text.p: Dutch flag carrier KLM said on Monday it signed an exclusive deal with tour operator Holland International to provide flights to holiday destinations.

"Starting April 1 next year, KLM will be the main flight supplier for Holland International," KLM spokesman Peter Wellhuner said. He said Holland International would use KLM on all its destinations where KLM flights were available.

Dutch newspaper De Telegraaf quoted Holland International director Ton Wendel saying the deal involved 60,000 passenger seats and would boost KLM's turnover by at least 50 million guilders but Wellhuner could not confirm this.
"These figures are Holland International's, and they (HI) are best able to judge on them. But whatever number of flights HI will ask us to supply, KLM has the capacity needed," he said.
Noone was available at Holland International for comment.
Holland International is part of Travel Unie, in which KLM has a nine percent stake, and was formed by the recent merger of Holland International and fellow Dutch travel group Arke.
The deal will run in principle for one year and is additional to other agreements between KLM and Travel Unie units, worth 450 to 500 million guilders a year, Wellhuner said.
